packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the fallback never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined [100,P1]

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, `selectedCalendar` is computed as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), but the predicate still compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null/""`). Unless a destinationCalendar entry also has that exact falsy externalId (unlikely/invalid), the find returns undefined, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and the code falls back to the default calendar ID later. This makes the fallback selection logic effectively broken and prevents using a provided destinationCalendar when `externalCalendarId` is not passed. The same flawed pattern is also introduced in deleteEvent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — identical dead `find` fallback in deleteEvent; delete issued with `calendarId: undefined` and `defaultCalendarId` computed but unused [100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `deleteEvent` logic computes `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` but then sets `calendarId` to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — previously-working `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback made permanently dead in updateEvent [90,P1]

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, the previous fallback `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (when destinationCalendar was a single object) was replaced with:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the case where the fallback is needed), the code searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will almost always return `undefined`. That makes the fallback effectively dead and can cause the update to target no calendar/incorrect default behavior. This is a concrete correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — same dead fallback in deleteEvent, so legacy references silently fail to delete from the right calendar [88,P1]

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the new fallback logic is effectively dead:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid calendar.
